disclaimer: Sample rules. Verify with local municipality.
source: Prototype sample rules based on general Indian waste-segregation practice. Not official CCMC guidelines.

rules.name: PET Plastic Bottle / Drink Container
rules.reason: Clear PET (#1) is highly in demand and easily recycled into new polyester yarn or bottles.

steps.prepare: Empty completely, rinse with minimal water, and let dry.
steps.separate: Remove cap (caps can be recycled separately). Flatten bottle to save collection bin space.
steps.route: Place into Dry/Recyclable bin or sell to dry waste aggregator / kabadiwala.

rules.name: Fruit & Vegetable Scraps
rules.reason: Quickly decomposes into nutrient-rich compost and prevents landfill methane emissions.

steps.prepare: Ensure free of stickers, plastic tags, or packaging.
steps.separate: Keep separate from dry plastic and paper waste.
steps.route: Put in Wet bin or add to home composter.

rules.name: Cooked Food Waste / Leftovers / Rice / Gravy
rules.reason: Biodegradable organic mass converted into biogas or compost by municipal wet waste processing plants.

steps.prepare: Drain excess liquid/gravy.
steps.separate: Keep separate from packaging and plastic wraps.
steps.route: Deposit in Wet bin on daily morning collection.

rules.name: Tea Bag / Tea Leaves
rules.reason: Tea leaves are rich in nitrogen, ideal for organic composting. (Check for plastic staples/synthetic mesh).

steps.prepare: Remove metal staple, tag, and string if synthetic.
steps.separate: If mesh bag is made of plastic/nylon, slit bag and discard leaves into Wet bin, nylon bag to Reject bin.
steps.route: Deposit organic leaves or unbleached paper tea bag in Wet bin.

rules.name: Eggshells
rules.reason: Excellent source of calcium and minerals for garden soil and compost piles.

steps.prepare: Crush lightly to accelerate composting.
steps.separate: Ensure no plastic packaging is mixed.
steps.route: Add to Wet bin or home garden compost.

rules.name: Coconut Shell / Husk
rules.reason: Dense organic biomass used for coco-peat, craft items, or slow composting / biochar.

steps.prepare: Remove any synthetic tags or twine.
steps.separate: Can be kept with garden waste or organic waste.
steps.route: Place in Wet bin or garden composter.

rules.name: Wooden Chopstick / Ice Cream Stick / Toothpick
rules.reason: Natural untreated wood is 100% biodegradable and composts into organic humus.

steps.prepare: Ensure no plastic coating or paint.
steps.separate: Place with organic waste.
steps.route: Place in Wet bin or garden composter.

rules.name: Used Household Battery (AA/AAA/Lithium)
rules.reason: Contains toxic heavy metals (lead, cadmium, lithium) that cause landfill fires and contaminate groundwater.

steps.prepare: Tape the terminals (+ and - ends) with clear tape to prevent short circuits.
steps.separate: Never mix with general wet or dry household waste.
steps.route: Drop off at designated Hazardous/E-waste drop-off center or authorized electronics recycler.

rules.name: Cardboard Pizza Box / Takeout Box
rules.clarifying_question: Is the cardboard greasy or food-soiled?

greasy.reason: Oil and food grease soak into paper fibers, preventing pulp separation at recycling mills. However, unlined cardboard is compostable.

steps.prepare: Tear off any clean, grease-free top lid portion.
steps.separate: Place the greasy bottom in the Wet bin / compost; put clean dry top in Dry/Recyclable bin.
steps.route: Greasy portions go to Wet bin or municipal composting.

clean.reason: Clean corrugated cardboard is high-grade recyclable material.

steps.prepare: Flatten the box completely.
steps.separate: Remove any leftover plastic sauce cups, wax paper, or staples.
steps.route: Place in Dry/Recyclable bin.

rules.reason: Recyclability depends strictly on whether grease or food oils have contaminated the paper fibers.

steps.prepare: Inspect for grease and food scraps.
steps.separate: Tear clean top for Dry/Recyclable bin, dirty bottom for Wet bin.
steps.route: Separate into Wet bin or Dry/Recyclable bin according to food contamination.

rules.name: Aluminum Beverage Can / Tin Can
rules.reason: Aluminum is infinitely 100% recyclable with 95% less energy than virgin mining.

steps.prepare: Empty liquid and rinse lightly.
steps.separate: Crush can if convenient.
steps.route: Place in Dry/Recyclable bin or sell to scrap dealer.

rules.name: Milk Pouch (LDPE Plastic Packet)
rules.reason: Low-Density Polyethylene (#4) is recyclable if cleaned and dry, but causes odor/contamination if unwashed.

steps.prepare: Cut the corner without fully detaching the tip (to avoid micro-plastic litter). Rinse thoroughly with water and let dry inside out.
steps.separate: Bundle multiple dry pouches inside one pouch.
steps.route: Hand over to Dry/Recyclable bin or specialized plastic collection drive.

rules.name: Glass Bottle / Glass Jar
rules.reason: Glass can be recycled endlessly without quality loss.

steps.prepare: Rinse clean and remove metal or plastic lids.
steps.separate: Keep intact. If broken, wrap carefully in thick newspaper and label 'Broken Glass' to protect sanitation workers.
steps.route: Place in Dry/Recyclable bin or return to deposit scheme / kabadiwala.

rules.name: Cardboard Shipping Box / Carton
rules.reason: High-grade recyclable fiber that is pulped into new corrugated shipping boxes.

steps.prepare: Remove plastic shipping tape, bubble wrap, and sticky address labels if plastic.
steps.separate: Flatten box completely.
steps.route: Place in Dry/Recyclable bin or sell to scrap dealer.

rules.name: Newspaper / Magazine / Office Paper
rules.reason: Clean paper fibers can be recycled 5 to 7 times into recycled paper products.

steps.prepare: Keep completely dry. Do not crumple tightly.
steps.separate: Stack and tie with twine.
steps.route: Place in Dry/Recyclable bin or sell directly to local paper recycler.

rules.name: Worn Clothes / Fabric Scraps / Old Textile
rules.reason: Textiles can be repurposed, downcycled into rags/insulation, or donated if still usable.

steps.prepare: Wash and dry properly.
steps.separate: If wearable, donate to charity. If torn/unusable, bundle separately.
steps.route: Place in Dry/Recyclable bin or cloth donation drive.

rules.name: Paper Cup / Disposable Coffee Cup
rules.reason: Most disposable paper cups have an internal waterproof polyethylene plastic lining that standard paper recycling facilities cannot separate easily.

steps.prepare: Empty remaining liquid completely.
steps.separate: Remove plastic lid and straw (if plastic lid is rigid, put lid in Dry/Recyclable bin).
steps.route: Place paper cup in Reject bin.

rules.name: Styrofoam / Expanded Polystyrene (EPS)
rules.reason: Thermocol is 98% air and extremely bulky; municipal mechanical recycling is rarely economically viable.

steps.prepare: Break into manageable pieces without scattering small beads.
steps.separate: Keep dry and separated from food waste.
steps.route: Place in Reject bin.

rules.name: Multi-Layer Snack Wrapper (Chips / Biscuit / MLP)
rules.reason: Multi-Layered Plastics (MLP) bond metallized plastic film and polymer, making mechanical recycling difficult.

steps.prepare: Empty all crumbs.
steps.separate: Collect in dry reject stream.
steps.route: Place in Reject bin - routed to cement kilns for energy recovery (RDF).

rules.name: Plastic Straw / Single-use Cutlery
rules.reason: Too lightweight and small to be sorted by automated sorting screens at Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs).

steps.prepare: Rinse off food residue.
steps.separate: Avoid using; switch to metal or bamboo alternatives.
steps.route: Place in Reject bin.

rules.name: Thin Plastic Carry Bag / Polythene Bag
rules.reason: Single-use thin plastic bags are restricted in many places. Avoid them.

steps.prepare: Clean and dry. Avoid taking single-use bags.
steps.separate: Group with soft plastics.
steps.route: Place in Reject bin.

rules.name: Medicine Blister Pack (Alu-PVC)
rules.reason: Tightly bonded layers of plastic (PVC) and aluminum foil cannot be separated by standard recyclers.

steps.prepare: Ensure expired medicines are removed (never flush medicines down drains).
steps.separate: Empty blister pack goes to reject waste.
steps.route: Place in Reject bin or pharmacy medicine return drive.

rules.name: Electronic Waste (Phone, Charger, Laptop, PCB)
rules.reason: Contains precious metals (gold, copper) along with toxic brominated flame retardants and heavy metals.

steps.prepare: Back up / wipe data if it is a smart device.
steps.separate: Store in a dry box away from rain and moisture.
steps.route: Drop off at Hazardous/E-waste drop-off center or authorized take-back kiosk.

rules.name: CFL / Tube Light / LED Bulb
rules.reason: CFLs and fluorescent tube lights contain toxic mercury vapor that releases if shattered. LED bulbs contain electronic driver circuits that belong in e-waste.

steps.prepare: Do not break the glass tube or bulb. Wrap in protective cardboard sleeve if possible.
steps.separate: Separate strictly from ordinary household waste.
steps.route: Drop off at Hazardous/E-waste drop-off center (CFL/tubes as hazardous, LEDs as e-waste).

rules.name: Aerosol Spray Can (Deodorant / Paint)
rules.reason: Pressurized can that can explode in compactor trucks or trash incinerators if heated or punctured.

steps.prepare: Do not puncture or burn.
steps.separate: Remove plastic nozzle cap.
steps.route: Hand over to Hazardous/E-waste drop-off collection.

rules.name: Sanitary Napkins / Diapers / Medical Bandages
rules.reason: Biohazard and non-recyclable; requires high-temperature municipal incineration.

steps.prepare: Wrap securely in newspaper or disposal pouch marked with a red cross mark.
steps.separate: Strictly do NOT mix with Wet bin or Dry/Recyclable bin.
steps.route: Hand over as Hazardous/Domestic special waste.

rules.name: Other Organic Waste / Food Scraps
rules.reason: Biodegradable organic matter suitable for composting and anaerobic digestion.

steps.prepare: Remove plastic packaging or synthetic wraps.
steps.separate: Keep separate from dry recyclables.
steps.route: Deposit in Wet bin (Green bin stream).

rules.name: Other Paper or Cardboard
rules.reason: Clean unsoiled paper fiber is pulped into new recycled paper products.

steps.prepare: Keep completely dry and grease-free.
steps.separate: Flatten and bundle.
steps.route: Place in Dry/Recyclable bin.

rules.name: Other Plastic Item
rules.reason: Recyclability depends on polymer code (#1 to #7) and local municipal facilities. Many mixed plastics are non-recyclable.

steps.prepare: Check the recycling number (1 to 7) and your local rules. Rinse and keep dry.
steps.separate: Keep separate from wet food waste.
steps.route: If resin number #1 (PET) or #2 (HDPE), place in Dry/Recyclable bin; otherwise place in Reject bin.

rules.name: Other Metal Item
rules.reason: Metals are highly recyclable with significant energy savings.

steps.prepare: Wipe clean of grease and oils.
steps.separate: Keep separate from general waste.
steps.route: Place in Dry/Recyclable bin or sell to scrap dealer.

rules.name: Other Electronic Item (Special Handling)
rules.reason: Electronic hardware contains valuable trace metals and toxic components requiring specialized recovery.

steps.prepare: Store safely in dry conditions.
steps.separate: Never mix with ordinary household trash.
steps.route: Drop off at authorized Hazardous/E-waste drop-off point.

default_fallback.reason: I'm not sure. Please retake the photo or describe the item.

steps.prepare: Inspect the item closely.
steps.separate: Check with local municipal guidelines.
steps.route: Retake photo or enter item name in text box.
